findings.evidence: Mathlib naming says theorem names describe the conclusion read outward; adjacent declarations are `energyIntegrand_zero_drift_flip_eq_of_isSymm` at `SymmetricEnergy.lean:72`, `energyIntegrand_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_flip_eq` at `SymmetricEnergy.lean:115`, and `isCoercive_energyIntegrand_zero_drift(_on)` at `UniformEllipticEnergy.lean:219,232`, while the new reversed forms occur at lines 57, 71, 97, 106, 119, and 129.
findings.fix: Rename along the existing local pattern, e.g. `energyIntegrand_zero_drift_flip_eq_and_isCoercive_of_isSymm`, `energyIntegrand_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_flip_eq_and_isCoercive`, and matching `..._on` namespace wrappers.
findings.issue: The paired names `zero_drift_flip_eq_and_isCoercive_energyIntegrand`, `coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_flip_eq_and_isCoercive_energyIntegrand`, and their `UniformlyEllipticOn`/`_on` variants put `energyIntegrand` at the end instead of naming the conclusion from the head expression outward.

summary: Several new theorem names put the object `energyIntegrand` after the conclusion fragments, breaking the adjacent PDE naming pattern and Mathlib’s conclusion-outward naming rule.
